summary: 76-year-old woman with 3 hours of palpitations, chest tightness and dizziness: AF 168/min, BP 78/50, confused. ESC 2024: emergency electrical cardioversion.

inputs.hpi: Three hours of a racing heartbeat, tightness across the chest, and feeling faint; now muddled. Known paroxysmal AF, stopped her apixaban last month because of bruising. Attending for a post-operative check after laparoscopic cholecystectomy 6 weeks ago.

exam.cardiovascular: Pulse 168 irregularly irregular, BP 78/50, cool peripheries.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response and haemodynamic instability
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Fast AF with hypotension, chest tightness and confusion - haemodynamically unstable: emergency transfer for synchronised DC cardioversion.

guideline.name: 2024 ESC Guidelines for the management of atrial fibrillation
guideline.section: AF-CARE: 12-lead ECG to confirm AF; emergency electrical cardioversion for haemodynamic instability; rate control (beta-blocker, diltiazem/verapamil, digoxin); stroke risk with CHA2DS2-VA - oral anticoagulation recommended for score >=2 and considered for 1; DOAC preferred over VKA; look for precipitants (thyroid function, infection)
guideline.citation: Van Gelder IC, Rienstra M, Bunting KV, et al. 2024 ESC Guidelines for the management of atrial fibrillation developed in collaboration with EACTS. Eur Heart J. 2024;45:3314-3414.

rationale: Unstable AF: the one AF situation where rate control and anticoagulation discussions must wait for electrical cardioversion.
